disclaimer: Level descriptions are Nalkudil Studio's independent maturity-model design, following the standard 5-level structure used in capability maturity frameworks (Ad Hoc → Managed → Defined → Quantified → Optimized). Not a certified or licensed framework — use as a structured self-assessment starting point.

questions.text: How is incident management handled?
levels: Incidents handled informally via email/chat, no ticketing system
Ticketing system in place but categorization is inconsistent
Standardized incident categorization and priority matrix documented and followed
Incident MTTR and SLA compliance tracked and reported monthly
Incident trends analyzed to proactively prevent recurrence; AI-assisted triage live

questions.text: How are changes to production systems managed?
levels: Changes made ad hoc with no approval process
Basic change requests logged but approval is informal
Formal Change Advisory Board (CAB) process with risk assessment
Change success/failure rates tracked, correlated to incident spikes
Automated change risk scoring with predictive rollback triggers

questions.text: How mature is your CMDB / asset management?
levels: No centralized asset inventory
Spreadsheet-based asset tracking, updated irregularly
Dedicated CMDB with defined CI relationships
CMDB accuracy audited regularly, drives capacity planning
CMDB auto-discovers and reconciles assets in real time

questions.text: How is knowledge management run?
levels: No knowledge base; tribal knowledge only
Informal KB articles exist but are outdated/unmaintained
KB is structured, reviewed on a schedule, tied to ticket resolution
KB usage and deflection rate measured against ticket volume
AI-curated KB auto-suggests and auto-updates from resolved tickets

questions.text: How are SLAs/OLAs defined and used?
levels: No formal SLAs defined
SLAs exist but are generic/not tiered by severity
SLAs tiered by priority/service, documented in contracts
SLA performance tracked and reported to stakeholders regularly
SLAs dynamically adjusted based on business-impact analytics

questions.text: How is your ITSM platform utilized?
levels: Multiple disconnected tools, no single system of record
Single ITSM tool adopted but only for ticketing
ITSM tool used across incident/change/problem/asset modules
ITSM data feeds executive dashboards and capacity decisions
ITSM platform is the automation backbone (workflows, AI, orchestration)

questions.text: What's your support channel strategy?
levels: Phone-only support
Phone + email, no unified queue
Omnichannel (phone/chat/email/portal) with unified queue
Channel performance (AHT, CSAT) tracked per channel
AI dynamically routes contacts to optimal channel based on complexity

questions.text: How is service desk staffing planned?
levels: Staffing based on gut feel / headcount inherited from budget
Basic headcount planning based on historical ticket counts
Erlang-based or similar workforce-management staffing model in use
Staffing model incorporates shrinkage, tiering, and forecasted volume
Staffing dynamically re-optimized using real-time automation-adjusted demand

questions.text: How is your tiering structure defined?
levels: Single-tier support, everyone handles everything
Informal L1/L2 split, unclear escalation criteria
Documented tiering with defined escalation/nesting ratio
Tier performance (FCR, escalation rate) tracked by tier
Tiering dynamically adjusts based on skill-based routing and AI triage

questions.text: How is First Contact Resolution (FCR) managed?
levels: FCR not measured
FCR estimated informally, not systematically tracked
FCR tracked as a formal KPI
FCR trends drive coaching and process improvement
FCR optimized via AI-assisted agent guidance in real time

questions.text: How is quality assurance and coaching run?
levels: No call/ticket quality review process
Ad hoc spot-checks by supervisors
Structured QA scorecards and regular coaching cycles
QA scores correlated with CSAT/FCR to guide targeted coaching
AI-assisted quality scoring across 100% of interactions

questions.text: How visible is your cost-to-serve?
levels: No visibility into cost per ticket/contact
Rough annual budget known, not broken down per ticket
Cost per ticket calculated by channel/tier
Cost-to-serve tracked against automation-driven savings targets
Real-time cost-to-serve dashboard drives staffing and tooling decisions

questions.text: How visible is employee device/app experience?
levels: No visibility into employee device/app experience
Reactive visibility only via helpdesk complaints
DEX/telemetry tooling deployed on majority of the estate
DEX data correlated with ticket volume and sentiment surveys
DEX-driven proactive remediation resolves issues before users notice

questions.text: How is employee sentiment measured?
levels: No employee sentiment data collected
Annual/occasional engagement surveys only
Regular XLA-style pulse surveys tied to IT services
Sentiment scores tracked as a governed KPI alongside SLAs
Sentiment predictively modeled from behavior/telemetry, not just surveys

questions.text: How proactive is issue remediation?
levels: All issues are reactive (user reports, then IT responds)
Some scripted remediations exist but are manually triggered
Automated remediation triggers on defined device health thresholds
Remediation success rate tracked and tuned
Predictive remediation resolves issues before symptoms appear

questions.text: How is device health and refresh managed?
levels: No visibility into device age/health across the estate
Device refresh based on fixed depreciation schedule only
Device health data informs refresh prioritization
Refresh ROI tracked against experience/productivity improvement
Refresh cycles dynamically optimized using DEX + cost data together

questions.text: How is SaaS/business app performance monitored?
levels: No monitoring of business-critical SaaS/app performance
Monitoring limited to infrastructure, not the app experience itself
End-to-end app experience monitored for critical business apps
App performance data tied to business-impact reporting
AI correlates app degradation to root cause across the full stack

questions.text: How is experience reported to leadership?
levels: No experience metrics reported to leadership
Ad hoc anecdotal reporting when issues escalate
Regular XPI/DEX scorecard presented to IT leadership
Experience scorecard tied to business outcomes (attrition, productivity)
Experience metrics are a standing board-level KPI

questions.text: How formal is your automation strategy?
levels: No automation strategy; automation is opportunistic/accidental
A few scripts/macros exist, undocumented and unowned
Formal automation roadmap tied to call-driver/ticket analysis
Automation ceiling and realized % tracked as a governed metric
Automation strategy dynamically re-prioritized using live ticket data

questions.text: How is self-service adopted?
levels: No self-service portal or catalog
Self-service portal exists but is rarely used
Self-service catalog covers top call drivers, actively promoted
Self-service deflection rate tracked and targeted
AI-driven self-service adapts in real time to emerging issues

questions.text: How mature is RPA/workflow automation?
levels: No RPA or workflow automation in use
A handful of isolated RPA bots, no governance
RPA/workflow automation governed with a CoE and reuse library
RPA ROI tracked per process automated
RPA orchestrated alongside AI agents in unified workflows

questions.text: How deployed is AI/Copilot in your operations?
levels: No AI/Copilot tools deployed
Pilot/trial of an AI copilot in one team
AI copilot deployed broadly for specific use cases (triage, KB)
AI copilot adoption and impact measured (deflection, AHT reduction)
AI agents autonomously resolve tickets end-to-end for defined categories

questions.text: How ready is your data for AI consumption?
levels: Ticket/KB data is messy, inconsistent, not AI-ready
Some data cleanup done, but no structured taxonomy
Data taxonomy standardized, KB structured for AI consumption
Data quality actively monitored and improved for AI accuracy
Data pipeline continuously feeds and retrains AI models

questions.text: How is automation governed?
levels: No ownership of automation initiatives
Individual teams own automation ad hoc, no central visibility
Central automation governance body tracks all initiatives
Automation portfolio prioritized using ROI/ceiling analysis
Automation governance integrated into overall IT strategy planning

questions.text: How is field dispatch managed?
levels: No formal dispatch process, ad hoc assignment
Manual dispatch based on technician availability only
Documented dispatch model with defined SLA windows (NBD, etc.)
Dispatch performance (SLA achievement, travel time) tracked
Dispatch dynamically optimized using hub-count/routing models

questions.text: How is your hub/coverage strategy designed?
levels: No defined coverage strategy, technicians assigned reactively
Coverage based on historical headcount, not modeled
Hub-and-spoke or coverage model formally designed
Coverage cost vs. SLA trade-off analyzed regularly
Coverage model re-optimized as volume/geography shifts

questions.text: How is VIP/executive support handled?
levels: No differentiated support for VIP/executive users
VIP support handled informally by whoever is available
Dedicated VIP queue/process with defined SLA
VIP SLA performance tracked separately from general queue
VIP support proactively monitored to prevent escalations

questions.text: How is walk-up/deskside coverage staffed?
levels: No walk-up support desk exists
Walk-up desk exists but coverage is inconsistent
Minimum staffing floor defined and maintained for walk-up desk
Walk-up demand vs. staffing floor tracked and adjusted
Walk-up coverage dynamically staffed based on real-time demand

questions.text: How is parts/inventory managed?
levels: No parts inventory tracking
Parts tracked informally, frequent stockouts
Parts/inventory carrying cost factored into hub economics
Inventory turns and stockout rate tracked as KPIs
Predictive inventory restocking tied to failure-rate analytics

questions.text: How is field technician utilization tracked?
levels: Technician utilization not tracked
Utilization estimated informally
Utilization tracked against a target occupancy benchmark
Utilization data drives headcount and territory adjustments
Utilization optimized in real time via dynamic routing

questions.text: How is patch management run?
levels: Patching is manual and inconsistent
Patch cycles exist but SLA compliance isn't tracked
Patch compliance tracked as a formal KPI with defined SLA
Patch compliance correlated with vulnerability/breach risk data
Patching is automated and risk-prioritized in real time

questions.text: How mature is vulnerability management?
levels: No formal vulnerability scanning
Vulnerability scans run occasionally, findings not tracked to closure
Regular scanning with tracked remediation SLAs
Vulnerability exposure quantified in business-risk/dollar terms
Vulnerability response is automated and continuously prioritized

questions.text: How complete is endpoint security coverage?
levels: Inconsistent or missing endpoint protection across the estate
Endpoint protection deployed but coverage/compliance not verified
Endpoint protection coverage verified and reported regularly
Endpoint security posture is a tracked executive KPI
Endpoint security integrated with DEX/automation for auto-remediation

questions.text: How is access governance handled?
levels: Access provisioned/revoked manually, no periodic review
Access reviews happen occasionally, inconsistently
Formal joiner-mover-leaver access governance process
Access governance audited and tracked against compliance standards
Access governance automated with continuous entitlement review

questions.text: How ready is your incident response process?
levels: No documented security incident response plan
A plan exists but hasn't been tested
IR plan tested via regular tabletop exercises
IR performance (detection/response time) measured
IR is automated/orchestrated with real-time threat intelligence

questions.text: How is security awareness and reporting run?
levels: No security awareness training program
Annual generic security training only
Regular, role-specific security awareness training
Security posture reported to leadership as a standing metric
Security posture is a board-level KPI tied to business risk

questions.text: How is vendor selection conducted?
levels: Vendors selected informally/relationship-based
Basic RFP process exists but criteria are inconsistent
Formal weighted RFP/scoring process used for major decisions
Vendor selection outcomes tracked against post-implementation performance
Vendor scoring model continuously refined using realized ROI data

questions.text: How is contract management run?
levels: Contracts tracked informally, renewal dates often missed
Central contract repository exists but isn't proactively managed
Contract renewals tracked with lead-time triggers for renegotiation
Contract terms benchmarked against market rates regularly
Contract portfolio optimized proactively across the vendor estate

questions.text: How is vendor performance managed?
levels: No formal vendor performance tracking
Vendor issues addressed reactively as they arise
Vendor SLAs tracked via regular business reviews
Vendor performance scorecards tied to contractual consequences
Vendor performance data feeds future sourcing decisions automatically

questions.text: How is multi-vendor coordination handled?
levels: No coordination between vendors supporting different towers
Vendors coordinate informally, gaps/overlaps common
Defined RACI/governance model across multi-vendor landscape
Cross-vendor performance measured against end-to-end SLAs
Multi-vendor ecosystem orchestrated via shared tooling/data

questions.text: How visible is total cost of ownership (TCO)?
levels: No visibility into full TCO of vendor relationships
Direct license/contract cost known, hidden costs not tracked
TCO modeled including implementation, support, and exit costs
TCO tracked over time against value delivered
TCO modeling drives dynamic sourcing/renewal decisions

questions.text: How prepared are you for vendor exit/transition?
levels: No exit strategy for critical vendors
Exit considered only reactively when a relationship fails
Exit/transition plans documented for critical vendors upfront
Exit readiness tested/reviewed periodically
Vendor portfolio actively hedged to minimize lock-in risk

questions.text: How are IT investments justified?
levels: IT investments approved without formal business cases
Basic cost estimates provided, benefits rarely quantified
Formal business cases with cost/benefit required for major investments
Business cases include NPV/ROI/payback analysis
Business case outcomes tracked post-launch and fed back into future cases

questions.text: How is IT budget tracked?
levels: IT budget tracked at a high level only, no line-item detail
Line-item budget exists but variance isn't analyzed
Budget vs. actual tracked and reviewed regularly
Budget variance root-caused and tied to specific initiatives
Budget dynamically reforecast using real-time cost/usage data

questions.text: How is cost avoidance measured?
levels: Cost avoidance from automation/efficiency isn't measured
Cost avoidance estimated informally, not validated
Cost avoidance calculated using a defined baseline methodology
Cost avoidance tracked against target and reported to finance
Cost avoidance modeling is continuously validated against actuals

questions.text: How is investment risk quantified?
levels: Project risks discussed informally, not quantified
Risks listed but not scored or prioritized
Risk register with likelihood/impact scoring used for major initiatives
Risk-adjusted ROI used in investment decisions
Risk models continuously updated using real incident/outcome data

questions.text: How is stakeholder financial reporting run?
levels: No regular financial reporting on IT initiatives to stakeholders
Ad hoc updates provided when asked
Regular financial/status reporting cadence established
Reporting includes leading indicators, not just lagging spend
Real-time financial dashboards available to all stakeholders

questions.text: How is the IT investment portfolio managed?
levels: Each IT initiative evaluated in isolation
Some awareness of overlapping initiatives, not formally managed
Portfolio view maintained across all major IT investments
Portfolio prioritized using consistent ROI/impact criteria
Portfolio dynamically rebalanced as new data/initiatives emerge
